theory.intro: Some circle problems need more than one property. A diagram can combine a chord property, an angle property and a cyclic quadrilateral property, sometimes side by side and sometimes with the result of one feeding into the next.
facts: Identify every configuration first — equal or perpendicular chords, central or circumference angles, a diameter, a cyclic quadrilateral.
A diameter gives the angle in a semicircle, and, because the centre lies on it, a chord perpendicular to it is bisected.

Equal chords give equal angles at the centre. They also give equal angles at the circumference when the angles stand on matching arcs or corresponding segments; angles standing on opposite choices of major and minor arcs can be supplementary.
Work one property at a time, using each result as an input to the next.
steps: List every chord, angle and quadrilateral configuration shown in the diagram.
Solve using the first property that can be applied directly from the given information.
Feed that result into the next applicable property.
Repeat until every unknown is found, and check the results are consistent (e.g. angles sum correctly).

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $\angle ABC=90^{\circ}$ because the angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
$\begin{aligned}AC&=2\times6.5=13\text{ cm}\\BC^2&=AC^2-AB^2\\&=13^2-12^2\\&=25\\BC&=5\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
(b) Again, $\angle ABC=90^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}\angle BCA&=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-42^{\circ}\\&=48^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The central angle and $\angle ACB$ stand on the same minor arc $AB$.
$\begin{aligned}\angle ACB&=\frac12\times\angle AOB\\&=\frac12\times104^{\circ}\\&=52^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$C$, $D$ and $E$ lie on a straight line.
$\begin{aligned}\angle ADC&=180^{\circ}-72^{\circ}\\&=108^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the opposite interior angle, so $\angle ABC=72^{\circ}$.
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
$\begin{aligned}\angle BCD&=180^{\circ}-98^{\circ}\\&=82^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
The smaller central angle and $\angle ABC$ stand on the same arc $ADC$.
$\begin{aligned}\angle AOC&=2\times\angle ABC\\&=2\times72^{\circ}\\&=144^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\angle ABD$ and $\angle ACD$ stand on the same arc $AD$, so they are equal.
$\angle ACD=43^{\circ}$.
Equal chords are equidistant from the centre. Therefore $OF=OE=6.4\text{ cm}$.

$\angle ABC$ stands on the major arc $AC$, so use the reflex central angle.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Reflex }\angle AOC&=360^{\circ}-138^{\circ}\\&=222^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=\frac12\times222^{\circ}\\&=111^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text: $AB$ is a diameter of a circle of radius $10$ cm. $C$ lies on the circle and $AC = 16$ cm. Find $BC$.
foundation.solution_text:
$AB = 2 \times 10 = 20$ cm
$\angle ACB = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$BC = \sqrt{AB^2-AC^2} = \sqrt{20^2-16^2} = \sqrt{144} = 12$ cm

foundation.question_text: $O$ is the centre of a circle. $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on the circle, with $C$ on the major arc $AB$. $\angle AOB = 94^{\circ}$. Find $\angle ACB$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\angle ACB = \angle AOB \div 2$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)
$\angle ACB = 94^{\circ} \div 2 = 47^{\circ}$

$\angle ABC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle, since $AC$ is a diameter)
$\angle BCA = 180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 35^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$)
$\angle BCA = 55^{\circ}$
$\angle ADC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle at $D$)
$\angle DCA = 180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 40^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ADC$)
$\angle DCA = 50^{\circ}$

foundation.question_text: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. $\angle BAD = 106^{\circ}$ and $\angle ADC = 67^{\circ}$. Find $\angle BCD$ and $\angle ABC$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\angle BCD = 180^{\circ}-106^{\circ} = 74^{\circ}$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary)
$\angle ABC = 180^{\circ}-67^{\circ} = 113^{\circ}$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary)

foundation.question_text: $AC$ is a diameter of a circle and $B$ lies on the circle. $\angle BAC = 37^{\circ}$. Find $\angle BCA$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\angle ABC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$\angle BCA = 180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-37^{\circ} = 53^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$)

foundation.question_text: $AC$ is a diameter of a circle of radius $8.5$ cm. $B$ lies on the circle and $AB = 8$ cm. Find $BC$.
foundation.solution_text:
$AC = 2 \times 8.5 = 17$ cm
$\angle ABC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$BC = \sqrt{AC^2-AB^2} = \sqrt{17^2-8^2} = \sqrt{225} = 15$ cm

development.question_text: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. Side $CD$ is extended beyond $D$ to $E$. $\angle ADE = 123^{\circ}$. Find $\angle ABC$.
development.solution_text:
$\angle ABC = \angle ADE$ (an exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the opposite interior angle)
$\angle ABC = 123^{\circ}$

development.question_text: $AB$ is a diameter of a circle of radius $12.5$ cm. $C$ lies on the circle and $AC = 24$ cm. Find $BC$.
development.solution_text:
$AB = 2 \times 12.5 = 25$ cm
$\angle ACB = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$BC = \sqrt{AB^2-AC^2} = \sqrt{25^2-24^2} = \sqrt{49} = 7$ cm

$\angle ADE = \angle ABC$ (the exterior angle at $D$ equals the opposite interior angle).
$\angle ABC = 75^{\circ}$
$\angle AOC = \angle ABC \times 2$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)
$x = 75^{\circ} \times 2 = 150^{\circ}$

development.question_text: $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie on a circle in that order. $\angle ABD = 48.5^{\circ}$. Find $\angle ACD$.
development.solution_text:
$\angle ACD = \angle ABD$ (angles at the circumference standing on the same arc $AD$ are equal)
$\angle ACD = 48.5^{\circ}$

development.question_text: $O$ is the centre of a circle. $AB$ and $CD$ are equal chords. $OE$ and $OF$ are perpendicular to $AB$ and $CD$ respectively. $OF = 8.6$ cm. Find $OE$.
development.solution_text:
$OE = OF$ (equal chords are equidistant from the centre)
$OE = 8.6$ cm

development.question_text:
$A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie on a circle with centre $O$ in that order. Side $CD$ is extended beyond $D$ to $E$.
The exterior angle $\angle ADE = 68.5^{\circ}$.
Find the smaller central angle $\angle AOC$.
development.solution_text:
$\angle ABC = \angle ADE = 68.5^{\circ}$ (an exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the opposite interior angle)
$\angle AOC = 2 \times \angle ABC$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)
$\angle AOC = 2 \times 68.5^{\circ} = 137^{\circ}$

mastery.solution_text:
$O$ lies on diameter $AC$, so $OM$ is part of the line $AC$.
Since $BD \perp AC$ at $M$, this means $OM \perp BD$ too.
The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so $M$ is the midpoint of $BD$.
$OM = OA - AM = 10 - 4 = 6$ cm
In right-angled $\triangle OMB$: $OB = 10$ cm (radius), $OM = 6$ cm
$BM = \sqrt{OB^2-OM^2} = \sqrt{100-36} = \sqrt{64} = 8$ cm
$BD = 2 \times BM = 16$ cm

mastery.question_text: $O$ is the centre of a circle. $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on the circle, with $B$ on the minor arc $AC$. The smaller angle $\angle AOC = 127^{\circ}$. Find $\angle ABC$, giving reasons.
mastery.solution_text:
Reflex $\angle AOC = 360^{\circ}-127^{\circ} = 233^{\circ}$ (angles in a revolution)
$\angle ABC = 233^{\circ} \div 2 = 116.5^{\circ}$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)

mastery.question_text: $O$ is the centre of a circle. $AB$ is a chord and $P$ lies on $AB$, with $OP \perp AB$. Prove that $\triangle OAP \equiv \triangle OBP$, hence prove that $AP = PB$.
mastery.solution_text:
In $\triangle OAP$ and $\triangle OBP$:
$\angle OPA = \angle OPB = 90^{\circ}$ (given)
$OA = OB$ (radii of the circle)
$OP$ is common.
$\therefore \triangle OAP \equiv \triangle OBP$ (RHS)
$\therefore AP = PB$ (matching sides in congruent triangles are equal)
